answer: Admission is a soil-scarce witness, not a stake auction. An applicant registers one juniper plot, a unique 32-byte land commitment hashed from a survey point and public key, and leaves a shale core: a signed 48-hour moisture-and-radio log whose TPM quote cannot be cloned. Nightly sortition sends 20 established auditors to the same dune grid cell to check that no second key filed a plot within 200 meters or reused a TPM endorsement. A collision burns both bonds and bars both keys for four epochs. Server farms share one bench and fail the radius check.
